query: If airlines eliminated the most common cabin-service complaints in the reviews, how much would the average Overall Rating improve?

per_column.name: primary_service_complaint_category
per_column.rationale: Directly targets the query: identifying the most common cabin-service complaints is the core grouping needed to estimate rating uplift. Values are well grounded in samples (seat_comfort for the seat-complaint review; 'unknown' correctly assigned to praise-only reviews).

per_column.name: complaint_frequency_pattern
per_column.rationale: Whether a complaint is systemic vs isolated is relevant to prioritising which complaints to eliminate. However, it is not well grounded per-row: a single review generally cannot support 'recurring_systemic_issue' or 'route_dependent', which require cross-review aggregation. Labelling the narrow-seat review 'recurring_systemic_issue' asserts more than the text states.

per_column.name: cabin_class
per_column.rationale: Largely redundant with the existing original 'Class' column, so adds little new leverage. Groundedness is also weak: sample rows are confidently assigned 'business'/'economy' where the review text gives no clear class signal (e.g. the 'business' assignment for the Jakarta-Singapore praise review is unwarranted).

per_column.name: aircraft_cabin_condition
per_column.rationale: Cabin condition is a distinct axis relevant to cabin-service quality and rating. Some values are grounded (outdated for the 'dreadful seats' review; modern for the well-maintained review), but several are asserted where the text is silent, and NULL is used appropriately for others. Mixed reliability.

per_column.name: cabin_crew_service_tone
per_column.rationale: Crew service tone is a genuine service-quality axis pertinent to the query. Grounded where crew is described (warm_attentive for welcoming crew), but 'robotic_rushed' assigned to the seat-complaint review that never mentions crew is an unsupported inference.

per_column.name: food_quality_consistency
per_column.rationale: Food service is one of the cabin-service dimensions the query cares about, providing a usable grouping axis. Values track the source well (high_varied_menu for food-praise reviews) and NULL is used sensibly when food is unmentioned.

per_column.name: multi_complaint_pattern
per_column.rationale: Distinguishing single vs multiple service issues supports estimating combined rating uplift from eliminating complaints. Reasonably grounded: no_major_complaint for praise reviews, single_primary_issue for the lone seat complaint.

judge.rationale: Most added columns give genuine, query-relevant axes for grouping cabin-service complaints and modelling their impact on Overall Rating; primary_service_complaint_category is especially on-point. Weaknesses: cabin_class largely duplicates the existing 'Class' column and adds little, and several columns (complaint_frequency_pattern, cabin_class, aircraft_cabin_condition, cabin_crew_service_tone) exhibit confident per-row assertions unsupported by silent source text—e.g. 'robotic_rushed' and 'recurring_systemic_issue' on a review mentioning neither crew nor recurrence. Groundedness is otherwise decent, with NULL used appropriately for silent rows.
